question:
This is the macro I use to make sure the column name isnt starting with a number

{% macro valid_column_name (column_name) %}
    {% if  column_name[:1]|int(-1) >= 0  %}
        {{ return("_" ~ column_name )  }}
    {% else %}
        {{ return( column_name ) }}
    {% endif %}

{% endmacro %}

and then i would call it like

select 22 as valid_column_name('1')

If anyone wants to improve on this macro feel free
title: DBT Jinja Convert Column Name if starts with a number
answer:
I think your macro is pretty fine. I you prefere to use regular expressions, you can thanks to the Python "re" module available in dbt. But your code would not be shorter. select 22 as valid_column_name('1') doesn't make a lot of sense because '1' is hardcoded in this example. What is your bigger use case?

With regexp, I would write something like the following:

{% macro valid_column_name(column_name) %}
    {% if modules.re.match('^\d', column_name) %}
        {{ return("_" ~ column_name) }}
    {% else %}
        {{ return(column_name) }}
    {% endif %}
{% endmacro %}
